svg.title: A first-to-two game has six terminal paths of unequal lengths and weights
svg.desc: Two players play independent rounds with no draws. Player A wins each round with probability two thirds and player B with probability one third. The game stops as soon as either player reaches two wins. Start branches to A and B. From A, AA is a terminal two-round path with probability four ninths, while AB continues. From B, BB is a terminal two-round path with probability one ninth, while BA continues. AB branches to terminal ABA with probability four twenty-sevenths and terminal ABB with probability two twenty-sevenths. BA branches to terminal BAA with probability four twenty-sevenths and terminal BAB with probability two twenty-sevenths. Every edge shows its own round probability. There are no edges after AA or BB. All six terminal path probabilities sum to one. A wins through AA, ABA or BAA, with total probability twenty twenty-sevenths. Four paths last three rounds, with total probability four ninths. Terminal paths are not equally likely.
